answer: Checks name a berth and a minute: its disc is presented at that wharf berth, scan sent within 10 min. Each identity custodies one disc for 90 days, its pitting mapped in the registry atlas; auditors align scans to the etched horizon line and measure its deepest pit, since resin casts fill that pit and miss the atlas depth by 0.4 mm or more. One disc cannot back two identities, since simultaneous calls name two berths; a mismatch voids both claims and forfeits each $25 deposit. It costs $40 once per disc, deposit back after the exit audit; 1,000 fakes tie up 1,000 distinct discs and $40,000.
